label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
**Subject: Tuesday club at Knocknacarra, and something I need to tell you before the 18th**

Dear Niamh,

I hope you're well. I'm writing before Wednesday's review meeting because I'd like you to have the latest numbers, and because I have something to own up to.

When you emailed on 30 October about pausing the club from January, I understood the reasons: low attendance and the rise in the hall insurance. I've been thinking about it since, and I want to tell you what has happened in the room since September.

We had five children most weeks at the start. By mid-October there were nine, and last Tuesday, 3 November, we had fourteen. The children are coming back, and they're bringing friends. Declan Moran at the Salthill Book Nook also gave us 120 books, mostly for the 6 to 9 age group, and a good number are in Irish, which the children have really enjoyed. There's a family of two sisters who came from Ukraine in October. The older girl now reads aloud to her younger sister in English at the end of each session. And a boy who wouldn't open a book at all in September asked me last week whether he could take two home. I'd say he's not the only one who's changed.

I'm not saying this to argue against your decision. I'm saying it because I think it's worth seeing the club as it is now, not as it was when the numbers were low. Stopping just as it's taken off would be a real pity, and I'd be glad to talk it through with you before the 18th.

Now the part I'm not proud of. A few weeks ago I met Orla Keane from the Corrib Courier at the farmers' market. She asked about my work, and I got carried away telling her about the club. I told her she could come along to a session with a photographer any Tuesday. I should have come to you first. I know that, and I'm sorry. I put you in an awkward position and I didn't give you the chance to decide. She's pencilled in for Tuesday 24 November, and I haven't confirmed anything beyond that.

I know policy means no photographs of the children without your sign-off and the parental consent forms, and I'm not asking you to go around that. I also think good local coverage could do the club a lot of good, but only if it's done properly and with your agreement.

So here's what I'd like to do, and I'll go along with whatever you decide:

- I'll ring Orla today and ask her to hold off on the visit until you've had a chance to decide. I don't want anything happening while you're still weighing it up.
- If you'd like the coverage to go ahead, I'll collect the consent forms from families myself and bring them to you before anyone is photographed. Nothing will happen without your say-so.
- If you'd rather not have press at all, I'll tell Orla that plainly and that will be the end of it.

I'd also be happy to bring the attendance sheets and a few notes about the sessions to Wednesday's meeting, if that would help. I'd like the review to have the full picture.

Thank you for taking the time to read this, and for everything you've done to get this club running. I'm sorry for going ahead without checking with you first. It won't happen again.

Warm regards,

[Your name]
[Phone number]
